title: stream-escrow-handshake-idempotent-toolcalls-and-server-idle-timeouts (openai-compat)
author: Maya Patel
description: This PR introduces a server-side short-lived escrow for in-flight streaming sessions together with a handshake that preserves idempotency for function/tool calls when clients disconnect and later reconnect. Motivation: we observed two classes of customer-visible failures when clients unexpectedly drop TCP/websocket connections during function-calling streams: (1) duplicated downstream tool calls on reconnects, and (2) long tail stalls from server resources retained indefinitely for abandoned sessions. This change implements: - an escrow object scoped to a stream session that holds pending tool-invocation decisions for a configurable grace window (default 30s) and is referenced by an idempotency key tied to the client handshake; - an explicit reconnect handshake message (X-Redwood-Reconnect: session=<id>;escrow=<escrow-id>) supported by the OpenAI compatibility layer to allow resume-or-abort semantics for clients that reattach within the grace window; - a server-configurable idle timeout policy that frees compute and KV cache if no reconnect occurs after the escrow window, with a backstop forced-abort path for long-running tool calls; - conservative default behavior: if a reconnect is observed with a matching idempotency key, pending tool calls are not re-executed and the client receives a deterministic resume token stream; if a reconnect fails or the escrow expires, the server returns a soft-abort event and best-effort cleanup is performed. The PR includes tests, adapter changes, and docs. Checklist: - [x] escrow lifecycle and store implementation - [x] OpenAI-compat handshake header + adapter translations - [x] unit + e2e tests for reconnect scenarios - [x] console telemetry hooks for escrow expirations - [x] docs and migration notes for clients

b2e7f12 feat(openai-adapter): accept X-Redwood-Reconnect header and translate to internal resume request

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Overall approach looks solid. A couple questions: how does this interact with existing KV prefix caching? Can we guarantee no double-exec on a race?

Maya Patel (author): Escrow holds a reference to the decision token; we only take the execution lock when escrow is resolved. For KV prefixes we attach a soft-lock; added note in session_controller and test to cover races.
Li Wei: Please add an e2e that simulates a reconnect while a tool call is in-flight to ensure we return a deterministic outcome. Also check telemetry labels for multi-tenant filtering.
Maya Patel (author): Added the in-flight reconnect e2e and updated telemetry to include org_id label. Tests are stable locally; CI flaked once and I added a deterministic clock to the harness.
Noah Singh: lgtm after addressing minor nit on header parsing (trim whitespace).
Diego Martinez: Approved. Verified smoke on staging (integration with python SDK sample).
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (flaky reconnect test retried once)
bench: warning (microbench showed 3% increased latency under pathological reconnect churn; flagged for follow-up)
release_notes: Add short-lived stream escrow and OpenAI-compat reconnect handshake to prevent duplicate tool calls and reclaim abandoned session resources. Default escrow window 30s; configurable via STREAM_ESCROW_WINDOW_MS. Backwards compatible for clients that do not send the X-Redwood-Reconnect header.
notes_for_ops: When rolling out to Dedicated clusters, increase health-checks to account for TTL eviction spikes. Monitor console metric escrow_expired and bench latency for reconnect churn. If customers rely on long-running client-side reconnect behavior, increase STREAM_ESCROW_WINDOW_MS accordingly.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: older clients may not send reconnect header and will receive soft-abort after escrow expiry; mitigation: server returns explicit soft-abort event and docs include migration snippet, and STREAM_ESCROW_WINDOW_MS is conservatively long by default.
testing_notes: Added deterministic clock to e2e harness to eliminate flakiness. Tests cover: reconnect-within-window, reconnect-after-window, concurrent-reconnect-wins, in-flight-toolcall-reconnect. Local stress run 10k reconnect cycles passed.
migration_instructions: Clients that need resume semantics should start sending X-Redwood-Reconnect: session=<id>;idempotency=<client-key>. SDKs updated in this release to provide helper wrappers. No DB migrations required.
changelog_section: API: streaming: add escrow/reconnect handshake for idempotent tool calls (openai-compat)
